county-councillor.body:
{{current_date}}

{{recipient_name}}
Oxfordshire County Council
{{recipient_address}}

{{recipient_title}},

I am writing to you as a resident of {{sender_area}}, in {{sender_ward}}, regarding the proposed White Horse Reservoir (Planning Inspectorate reference WA010005).

As you will be aware, Oxfordshire County Council is a statutory consultee and the highway authority for the roads that would carry the bulk of the construction traffic for this project. I am grateful for the council's stance in its statutory consultation response of January 2026, which said it cannot support the application in its current form, and for calling the targeted consultation inadequate under the Gunning Principles.

I am writing to ask you to:

1. Continue to press Thames Water and the Planning Inspectorate to delay the DCO submission until a full and compliant consultation has been carried out.
2. Ensure that the council's Local Impact Report at examination stage is thorough and covers impacts on roads in {{sender_area}}, including the specific access points identified in the September 2026 targeted consultation.
3. Seek binding commitments on construction traffic routing and HGV restrictions through the Code of Construction Practice.

The access points now number seventeen, and Thames Water has admitted that construction traffic will be higher than previously forecast. The community in {{sender_area}} needs robust representation from the county council.

I would welcome a response setting out what actions the council is taking.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]

defra-secretary-of-state.title: Letter to the Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
defra-secretary-of-state.note: Emma Reynolds MP (High Wycombe) is Secretary of State as at November 2026. Update this frontmatter when the minister changes.
defra-secretary-of-state.body:
{{current_date}}

{{recipient_name}}
Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
{{recipient_address}}

{{recipient_title}},

I am writing to you as a resident of {{sender_area}}, in {{sender_constituency}}, regarding the proposed White Horse Reservoir (Planning Inspectorate reference WA010005). I am deeply concerned about the project's escalating costs, the adequacy of the consultation process, and the impact on my community.

The estimated cost of the project has risen from £2.2bn to £7.5bn. This dramatic escalation significantly undermines the business case and risks leaving bill payers and the public purse liable. I urge you to commission an independent review of the project's value for money and to require a genuine reassessment of alternatives, including the Severn-Thames Transfer scheme, before the Development Consent Order application is determined.

Oxfordshire County Council has stated, in its statutory consultation response, that it cannot support the application in its current form due to significant environmental impacts. The council has also said that the targeted consultation on access points fails to meet three of the four Gunning Principles, and has called for the DCO submission to be delayed. I share these concerns. The consultation process has not given local residents a proper opportunity to engage with the proposals.

Construction of the reservoir would last more than ten years and would bring large numbers of heavy goods vehicles through villages across the area, including {{sender_area}}. The number of access points has risen from six to seventeen in September 2026 alone. The impacts on road safety, air quality, and quality of life are severe and have not been properly assessed. I ask you to ensure that no DCO application is accepted until these concerns have been addressed and a further round of consultation has been held.

I would welcome a response setting out the steps your department intends to take.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]

district-councillor.body:

{{recipient_name}}
{{recipient_address}}

I am writing to you as a resident of {{sender_area}}, in {{sender_ward}}, regarding the proposed White Horse Reservoir (Planning Inspectorate reference WA010005).

I understand that Vale of White Horse District Council has formally objected to the reservoir and that the Leader has written to Defra calling for intervention on costs and a reassessment of alternatives. I am grateful for the council's strong position and I write to encourage you to continue this work.

I ask you to:

1. Ensure the council produces a thorough Local Impact Report at examination stage, covering the specific impacts on {{sender_area}} and neighbouring communities.
2. Press Thames Water for binding commitments on construction traffic management, including daily HGV limits, prohibited routes through residential streets, and out-of-hours restrictions.
3. Continue to call for an independent review of the project's value for money and a genuine reassessment of alternatives to the reservoir.

The recent rise in access points from six to seventeen means that the impacts on {{sender_area}} and the wider district are significantly greater than previously described. Residents deserve to know that the council is pressing hard for every available protection.

Thank you for the work you have already done on this issue. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]

foi-missing-minutes.title: Request for missing meeting minutes
foi-missing-minutes.note: Use this template to request missing minutes from a parish council, district council or county council. Adapt the body to name the specific meeting(s) and the authority. This is general information, not legal advice.
foi-missing-minutes.body:
{{current_date}}

{{recipient_name}}
{{recipient_address}}

{{recipient_title}},

**Request for minutes of [name the meeting(s) here, e.g. 'the parish council meeting of [date]']**

I am writing to request a copy of the minutes of the meeting(s) listed above, which do not appear to have been published on the council's website.

**Legal basis**

This request is made on the following grounds:

1. **Transparency Code for Smaller Authorities (2014):** parish councils and parish meetings with annual turnover up to £25,000 must publish draft minutes of formal meetings within one month of the meeting, free of charge and in an accessible format online.

2. **Freedom of Information Act 2000:** I am entitled to request recorded information held by the authority. The authority must respond within 20 working days of receiving this request. The authority's publication scheme (normally the ICO model publication scheme) covers minutes of formal meetings.

3. **Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR):** where the minutes contain information relating to environmental matters (including discussion of the White Horse Reservoir or other planning and infrastructure matters), they fall within the scope of the EIR. Requests under the EIR may be made verbally or in writing, and the authority must respond within 20 working days.

**This is general information, not legal advice.** If the authority refuses to provide the minutes or fails to respond within the statutory time limit, you may escalate to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk.

Please confirm receipt of this request. I ask that you treat it as a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and/or the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, as appropriate, and provide the minutes within 20 working days.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]

{{current_date}}

{{recipient_name}} MP
House of Commons
London SW1A 0AA

{{recipient_title}},

I am writing to you as one of your constituents, living in {{sender_area}}, {{sender_constituency}}, regarding the proposed White Horse Reservoir (Planning Inspectorate reference WA010005).

Thames Water expects to submit a Development Consent Order (DCO) application for a 150-billion-litre reservoir south-west of Abingdon in November 2026. This would be a nationally significant infrastructure project affecting my community for more than a decade of construction. The number of construction access points has risen from six to seventeen in September 2026 alone, and Thames Water has admitted that overall construction traffic will be higher than previously forecast.

I am concerned about the following:

1. The cost of the scheme has risen from £2.2bn to £7.5bn, significantly undermining the business case.
2. Oxfordshire County Council has said the targeted consultation fails to meet three of the four Gunning Principles and has called for the DCO submission to be delayed.
3. There has been no adequate assessment of alternatives, including the Severn-Thames Transfer scheme.
4. Construction traffic would pass through {{sender_area}} and neighbouring villages for more than a decade.

I would be grateful if you could raise these concerns with the Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, support calls for an independent review of the project's value for money, and press for a further round of public consultation before any DCO application is accepted.

Please let me know what steps you are taking on this issue.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]

ofwat.title: Letter to Ofwat
ofwat.recipient_address: Ofwat, Centre City Tower, 7 Hill Street, Birmingham, B5 4UA
ofwat.note: David Black is CEO of Ofwat as at November 2026. Update this frontmatter when the officer changes.
ofwat.body:
{{current_date}}

{{recipient_name}}
Chief Executive
Ofwat
{{recipient_address}}

{{recipient_title}},

I am writing to you as a resident of {{sender_area}}, in {{sender_constituency}}, regarding the proposed White Horse Reservoir and the RAPID gated process (Planning Inspectorate reference WA010005).

I understand that RAPID gate three was confirmed in May 2026, and that gate four is expected in January 2027. I am writing to ask Ofwat to use the RAPID process to require a more thorough assessment of value for money and of alternatives before the project progresses further.

The estimated cost of the project has risen from £2.2bn to £7.5bn. This is a more than threefold increase, and it significantly weakens the case for the scheme compared with alternatives such as the Severn-Thames Transfer, water efficiency investment, and smaller distributed storage options. I note that the Water Resources South East regional plan selected the reservoir but that RAPID required the three companies to update their best value assessment through the WRMP29 cycle. I ask that Ofwat makes the outcome of that assessment publicly available before gate four is confirmed.

I also ask Ofwat to clarify how bill payers across the three companies' areas will be protected if the project's costs continue to rise, and how it will ensure that the separately licensed Infrastructure Provider model does not insulate Thames Water from accountability for the scheme's impact on customers.

I would welcome a response setting out Ofwat's position on these points.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]

planning-inspectorate-relevant-represent.body:
WHITE HORSE RESERVOIR DEVELOPMENT CONSENT ORDER (WA010005)
RELEVANT REPRESENTATION

{{current_date}}

Name: [Your name]
Address: [Your address]
{{sender_area}}, {{sender_constituency}}

I submit this Relevant Representation in response to the application by Thames Water Utilities Ltd for a Development Consent Order for the White Horse Reservoir (WA010005).

I am a resident of {{sender_area}} and I have a direct interest in this application because [describe your interest: e.g. my property is near a construction access route / I use the affected roads regularly / my home is within the draft Order limits].

CONSTRUCTION TRAFFIC

The number of construction access points increased from six to seventeen in September 2026. Thames Water has acknowledged that overall construction traffic movements will be higher than previously forecast. This increase will directly affect roads in and near {{sender_area}}. I ask the Examining Authority to scrutinise closely:

- the traffic modelling for each access point, and whether it reflects the full increase from six to seventeen points;
- the proposed Code of Construction Practice, and whether it contains binding routing restrictions and HGV limits;
- the cumulative impact on roads in {{sender_area}}.

CONSULTATION ADEQUACY

Oxfordshire County Council has stated that the targeted consultation on access points failed to meet three of the four Gunning Principles. I am concerned that the Environmental Statement may not adequately address the impacts identified by local residents and councils during that consultation.

OTHER CONCERNS

[Add any further concerns relevant to your property or community, such as flood risk, noise, rights of way diversions, or impacts on a named local road.]

I ask that I am registered as an Interested Party and notified of all future examination deadlines.

Signed: [Your name]
Date: {{current_date}}

thames-water.title: Letter to Thames Water
thames-water.recipient_address: Thames Water Utilities Ltd, Clearwater Court, Vastern Road, Reading, RG1 8DB
thames-water.note: Cathryn Ross is CEO of Thames Water as at November 2026. Update this frontmatter when the officer changes.
thames-water.body:
{{current_date}}

{{recipient_name}}
Chief Executive Officer
Thames Water Utilities Ltd
{{recipient_address}}

{{recipient_title}},

I am writing to you as a resident of {{sender_area}}, in {{sender_constituency}}, regarding the proposed White Horse Reservoir (Planning Inspectorate reference WA010005).

I am writing before the Development Consent Order application is submitted to set out my concerns and to ask Thames Water to take specific steps to address them.

The increase in access points from six to seventeen in September 2026 has come as a shock to many affected communities. Thames Water has acknowledged that overall construction traffic will be higher than previously forecast, yet the targeted consultation that followed was criticised by Oxfordshire County Council for failing to meet three of the four Gunning Principles. Residents in {{sender_area}} have had insufficient opportunity to understand, comment on, and propose mitigations for the impacts of the additional access points on their daily lives.

I ask Thames Water to:

1. Delay the DCO submission until a full and compliant further consultation on access points has been carried out.
2. Publish detailed traffic modelling for each of the seventeen access points, showing peak HGV movements per hour on every affected road.
3. Commit to binding routing restrictions, daily HGV limits, and out-of-hours restrictions as part of the Code of Construction Practice.
4. Establish a residents' community liaison group, separate from the Technical Liaison Group, so that those living near construction routes have a direct voice throughout the build.

I look forward to receiving a substantive response.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your address]
